measurement_layers.log_metadata: Task-4 chronology and log-only variables (null when no CSV)

rubric_gaps_for_student.label: Peer-taught threshold value (peer as knowledge source)
rubric_gaps_for_student.why_not_covered: Section 6 currently defines scaffolded speech as teacher/researcher utterances. It does not explicitly address peer utterances. The implicit assumption is that peer-supplied information has the same status as teacher scaffolding (should not satisfy learner criteria). However, peer challenges (David's case) are different from peer instruction: a peer challenge where the learner defends or adjusts their model is more similar to learner-initiated reasoning than to a teacher scaffold.

rubric_gaps_for_student.label: Precision metric awareness (metric outside rubric scope)
rubric_gaps_for_student.why_not_covered: The rubric defines B8 in terms of MCR, sensitivity, and accuracy. B13 requires MCR + sensitivity integration specifically. Precision questions fall outside both. There is no rule for awareness of metrics beyond the CTR display. This is notable because precision-recall trade-off awareness is a legitimate AI literacy concept (UNESCO AI-CFT: 'understanding limitations of classification metrics').

rubric_gaps_for_student.label: Editing an existing CTR record (in-place model revision)
rubric_gaps_for_student.why_not_covered: CTR record editing is not described in B7 (which assumes build→emit→rebuild). The current rubric implies CTR is append-only. In-place editing of a historical row means the CTR log no longer reflects the build history accurately. No rule addresses: (a) whether in-place edits count as B7-D1 refinement evidence; (b) whether the edited row still counts as a separate model for B12 comparison.
